text:
Alex: heads-up — during the canary this morning we saw a p99 token latency spike tied to KV spills. tenant-42 accounted for ~62% of pagewalks in the window :eyes:
Marie: ugh. any clear root? heavy longctx?
Dan: digging through pprof and the slab stats now. preliminary: lots of small hot segments getting repeatedly evicted+reinstated, high fragmentation -> pagewalk thrash. attaching short pprof snippet below.
Dan: ```
(pprof) top10
50.2%  runtime.pagewalk
18.1%  runtime.kv_evict
10.4%  runtime.kv_reclaim
```
Luis: interesting — tenant-42 traffic is a mix of longctx + token streaming. their median seq len is 1.2k but the tail hits 8k. our current residency heuristic pins by allocated pages not access recency, so large longctx bursts push out many small hot entries.
Marie: so noisy neighbor via residency eviction rather than raw qps. can we soft-quota by resident-pages-per-tenant?
Alex: we already have a soft quota but it only enforces at allocation time; it doesn't account for fragmentation or reuse age. Result: tenant gets pages scattered across slabs and wins eviction races.
Dan: quick experiment idea: sampling-based decay + contiguous-bucket accounting. instead of counting pages, track a moving-window sample of active keys per tenant and an "age score" for reuse; score = alpha * recent_hits + beta * (1 / pages_allocated). When score low -> deprioritize residency retention.
Luis: prototype config I tried locally: ```json
{
  "tenant_quota_mode": "score_based",
  "score_alpha": 0.7,
  "score_beta": 0.3,
  "sample_window_seconds": 60,
  "evict_batch_size": 32
}
```
Dan: also saw a perf regression after the kernel-selection change last week: new memcpy kernel slightly increased pagewalk cost for small pages due to alignment. Reverting that kernel for pagewalk path reduced p99 by ~12% in canary.
Marie: action items?
Alex: 1) rollback kernel change for pagewalk path in canary (in progress by infra-bot). 2) run score-based quota experiment in a small canary (tenant-42 + 5 synthetic noisy tenants). 3) add fragmentation metric to console (per-tenant avg-contiguous-run-length).
Luis: I'll sketch the experiment and the lightweight sampling code. want to keep it cheap — don't change slab allocator, just sampling + eviction policy.
Dan: I'll add a pprof tag around pagewalk to isolate any remaining kernel regressions.
Marie: add alerts: sudden delta in per-tenant "resident pages" vs "active sample" > 3x. that would have flagged this earlier.
Alex: infra-bot? status on the rollback deploy?
infra-bot: rollback job queued: job-id 78910. will deploy canary in us-west-2 in ~7m. monitoring hooks: /alerts will be muted for 5m during deploy to avoid noise.
Marie: thanks. once canary looks stable we can run the 24h sampling canary and compare eviction churn and p99 tokens.
Luis: quick note — fragmentation mitigation ideas: 1) coalesce small pages into contiguous buckets for residency accounting; 2) prefer evicting from high-frag tenants first; 3) opportunistic compaction during low-load windows. I'll add a short doc.
Alex: perfect. keep notes in the experiment doc and post results in this thread. low-churn, measurable steps. :thumbsup:
Marie: tagging @eng-sre to watch the canary.
Dan: copying the pprof link for context: https://pprof.internal/redwood/2143216789/capture
Alex: thanks all — follow-ups: add console chart, run canary, and ship sampling patch to staging by EOD.
Luis: will do.
Alex: closing the loop later with the metrics diff. :party_parrot:
